result:
I’d make **curiosity stronger than contempt**—especially toward people we disagree with.

Not the kind that means “every idea is equally valid,” but the kind that asks, “What did this person experience that I haven’t?” before deciding they’re ignorant or malicious.

A lot of cruelty begins when disagreement turns into a judgment on someone’s character. If more people slowed down long enough to understand each other—not agree, just understand—arguments would become less personal and more useful. We could still be passionate and firmly opposed, without making opponents into enemies.

It wouldn’t solve every problem. It might make fewer people feel justified for becoming the problem.
